title: Intention-based economic alternatives and provider neutrality
summary: An intention expresses the desired outcome, permissible transformations and hard constraints. The planner should ask native Generalized Compute Intentions, WLU and allocator for valid execution alternatives, not invent compatible hardware, software, transports or legal routes.
invariants: The cheapest valid plan is not necessarily the cheapest machine.
Parallelization, data partitioning, memory segmentation, checkpointing, waiting and migration are admissible only when the actual workload/runtime declares them.
Intentions produce candidates, not irrevocable commercial entitlements.
Do not make Queue Fabric compulsory when direct invocation or JSON-RPC meets the semantic contract.

provenance.claim: Cloud Economics v0.1-dev8 source evidence; status=IMPLEMENTED.

procedure: Discover the job's computation, duration, memory model and portability capabilities.
Obtain hard veto/eligibility decisions from the upstream intention route.
Produce alternative feasible plans for single, distributed, defer and migrate strategies.
Rank on full total marginal cost, risk, completion and policy constraints.
Explain excluded cheap plans with exact evidence and reason.
